#   ⚠️ THIS DATE IS THE OLDEST LIVE-AND-TRACKED VECTOR'S 'Last Updated', **NOT** THE DATE OF THE LAST EDIT.
#   That is the whole point of a two-clock header. The clocks now disagree by ~5 WEEKS (they were SEVEN MONTHS apart
#   when this header was installed on 2026-08-21 — the gap closed because the tail was worked, not because the
#   stamp was edited):
#       clock 1 — oldest live tracked row : 2026-08-21  (VX-MARCO-2.01, 2.03, APT-01, AZ-01, ENF-01, H2A-01 …)
#       clock 2 — last edit to this file  : 2026-09-24
#   Dating the ledger by clock 2 would let a single refreshed row certify 56 unrefreshed ones. A ledger is
#   only as fresh as its STALEST LIVE ROW (finding_header_edit_is_the_edit_most_mistaken_for_maintenance).
#   ⚠️ It remains a FLOOR, not a summary. Distribution of the 29 live-and-TRACKED rows (9/24 s30c) is Sep 20 · Aug 9 · Jul 0 —

#   EVERY tracked row is within ~5 weeks; the >60d 'other' bucket re-filled to 4 by 9/24 (REM-02, EMG-01, FL-01, 2.06) and was worked back to EMPTY that day, and the five 7/31 rows were refreshed the same day (s31). The 6 rows
#   the staleness check still lists are ALL stale-BY-DESIGN. (36 live rows total; 7 of those are stale-BY-DESIGN — annual
#   Census/CBO cadence or no live primary — and are excluded from clock 1 because their age is intended.
#   The remaining 21 rows are FROZEN/RETIRED and are excluded from staleness entirely. 2026-08-21 s23: 37->36 live
#   / 20->21 retired — VX-2.05 (Agricultural Wage Growth) RETIRED, its primary permanently cancelled (NASS Farm
#   Labor Survey, Aug-2025) with no successor. Retired rather than left stale: a maintained band set for a
#   quantity nobody can measure is a standing invitation to substitute a proxy.)
#   2026-08-21: clock 1 moved 2026-01-22 -> 2026-02-24 -> 2026-07-02 as the whole >60d tail was worked in one
#     session: TX-01 + AZ-01 (211d, Realtor.com), TAX-01 (178d, NV Gaming Control Board primary PDF),
#     H2A-02 (82d, REBUILT as a measurement off OFLC date fields), ENF-01 (151d), APT-01 (67d, MIA primary).
#     ⚠️ NOT ONE of those five was merely old — each was carrying a reversed claim, an unscorable band, a
#     name/metric mismatch, a partial-vs-full-month artifact, or a dead source route. Staleness was the SYMPTOM.
#   HOW TO UPDATE: recompute clock 1 after any refresh — it moves only when the OLDEST tracked row moves,
#   which usually means it does NOT move when you refresh a fresh row. That is correct behaviour, not a bug.
# ==== GRADING CONVENTION (added 2026-08-21 s23 — READ BEFORE MARKING ANY ROW) ====
#   Every rule below exists because a hand audit of all 37 live rows found the same few
#   mechanical defects over and over: 35 of 37 carried at least one, and only VX-1.03 and
#   VX-H2A-02 were disjoint-and-exhaustive as written. The audit named a witness VALUE for
#   each claim (→ domain/sources/_archive/S23_BAND_AUDIT_2026-08-21.md); three witnesses are
#   LIVE current values, not hypotheticals. These five rules resolve the mechanical classes
#   ledger-wide in one place. They do NOT resolve missing bases or coverage gaps — those are
#   per-row work, tracked in the audit.
#   1. HIGHEST SATISFIED BAND WINS. Many rows are unbounded > chains (">10% decline" /
#      ">20%" / ">25%"), so a severe value satisfies two or three bands at once. WITNESS:
#      VX-1.01's live -28.9% 2-yr stack satisfies ELEVATED, CRITICAL *and* BREACHED.
#      Grade to the most severe satisfied band. This ratifies how rows were already being
#      marked — every mark checked at adoption was already the highest satisfied band, so
#      the rule changed NO status. It removes grader discretion, not marks.
#   2. A BOUNDARY VALUE BELONGS TO THE MORE SEVERE BAND. Ranges are half-open upward in
#      severity: "5-15% below" means [5,15). ~12 rows state closed-closed ranges that touch
#      ("within 5%" beside "5-15%"), putting the boundary in two bands at exactly the
#      numbers most likely to be argued.
#   3. A VALUE IN NO BAND IS **UNSCORED** — record it as UNSCORED and say so. NEVER round it
#      into the nearest band. Gaps are real and reachable: VX-1.01 has no band for a YoY
#      *increase* (live: +10.2%); VX-2.01 covers nothing between 0 and +25%; VX-2.04 covers
#      nothing between -100K and -200K; VX-FL-02/TX-01 cover nothing below 3 months supply.
#      UNSCORED is a finding about the spec. A rounded mark hides it forever.
#   4. ">-N%" MEANS A DECLINE DEEPER THAN N%, never "greater than -N%". Read literally, the
#      arithmetic sense makes BREACHED fire on healthy values. WITNESS: VX-TX-02's BREACHED
#      reads ">-10% YoY" and its live -5.71% satisfies it arithmetically. Prefer writing
#      "decline >10%" in new bands; this rule governs the legacy cells.
#   5. A BAND MUST NAME ITS BASIS AND ITS OBSERVATION WINDOW, in the NORMAL cell. Silence
#      here is the defect that survives longest, because the row still marks and the mark
#      still looks reasoned. WITNESSES: VX-1.01's bands say "YoY" while the row's own text
#      says the scoring basis is the 2-YR STACK — and the two disagree in SIGN today
#      (YoY +10.2%, stack -28.9%). VX-TAX-01's "±5% YoY" never says month or fiscal year —
#      monthly -6.99% grades ELEVATED, annual +5.07% grades UNSCORED (rule 3), and the row
#      is marked NORMAL. Until a row's bands name the basis, the basis is whatever its
#      Current Value explicitly names as the scoring basis; a row naming none is UNSCORED.
# ⚠️ PARSERS: the header row is BELOW this banner. Do not use `readline()` for the header (it returns this
